title: Traveling-wave MZM EO bandwidth
description: Electro-optic bandwidth of the traveling-wave MZM (models/optical_power/mzm_tw.va): a 50 Gb/s NRZ PRBS drives the distributed electrode of MZM at quadrature (vpi=1.5, vbias=0.75) and PD detects the optical output. On top of the quasi-static cos() transfer, mzm_tw imposes the two effects that set a real TW electrode's EO bandwidth: frequency-dependent electrode loss (pole at f_el = 35 GHz) and optical/RF velocity walk-off (pole at 0.443*c/(|n_rf-n_opt|*len) ~ 18 GHz for the default n_rf=2.4 vs n_opt=4.2 electrode). Their cascade gives an EO -3 dB bandwidth of ~15 GHz, so the 50 Gb/s optical eye (popt) and received eye (vout) are heavily closed. Set MZM.n_rf = 4.2 (velocity-matched) and re-run: the walk-off pole vanishes, only f_el limits (-3 dB ~ 35 GHz), and the eye springs open. The pinned physics studies are examples/mzm_tw_transient.py (step response + eye) and examples/mzm_tw_eo_bw.py (the network-analyser |H(f)| sweep).
